rows.backtranslation: A copy of the image is stored automatically and separately from an earlier time. Restore it: I cannot do it.

caller_contract.scope: Catch of Exception while restoring existing autosave ZIP through read/metadata/image/history/floating selection/credits/settings. This is not only missing file or pixel decoding. The initial previous automatically stored copy description is independent of which restoration step failed. It does not promise prior storage was valid/intact or claim no image has already been partially restored.

source_entries.title: Wall and Morgan, Navajo-English Dictionary (1958), printed57 / PDF64, right column
source_entries.sense: Exact full adverb tʼáá bíniʼdii has automatically as an explicit dictionary sense. The same entry also has uncontrolled, unchecked, unattended, uninhabited and unsettled senses. Polysemy does not erase the automatic sense; contextual selection and program-autonomy extension remain authored.
source_entries.limits: Own high-resolution raster reading: first i of bíniʼdii has acute, second is plain i; final dii has two plain i. Apostrophes normalized to U+02BC. Initial OCR/temporary unaccented bini and search-text biní readings are not used. No asserted 1958/1972 tone contrast.

source_entries.title: Wilson1994, printed99 / retained PDF56, PUT IT AWAY
source_entries.sense: PUT IT AWAY tells the reader to put hashtʼeʼ before SET IT DOWN. This supplies a storage/safekeeping modifier, not rescue/salvation.
source_entries.limits: Combining the modifier with the complete positional state siłtsooz is an existing reviewed project composition, not verb conjugation generated from an imperative.

source_entries.title: Wall and Morgan1958, printed52 / PDF59, nináádooltsos hashtʼeʼ
source_entries.sense: The dictionary explicitly associates hashtʼeʼ with a flat flexible object put away for safekeeping. The source future/again form is not used as a new completed-save verb.
source_entries.limits: The candidate inherits the bounded whole-image/document-as-sheet metaphor. It is not valid for all Save callers.

source_entries.title: Wall and Morgan1958 Navajo-English Dictionary, printed16/PDF23, right column
source_entries.sense: that which is the copy of, image of
source_entries.grammar: A complete possessed nominal expression supplied by the source, not a noun generated from COPY MACHINE. The source also lists beʼelyaago immediately above. The new noun phrase places existing image noun Eʼelyaaígíí before this copy-of nominal.
source_entries.limits: The noun is polysemous between copy and image/representation. It does not lexically mean rough draft, incomplete artwork, recoverable state, file, or bitmap. Copying a digital image is the authored extension; the new separate and automatic modifiers identify the auxiliary-copy relation.

source_entries.title: Wilson1994 Conversational Navajo Dictionary, printed106/PDF60, SEPARATELY
source_entries.grammar: The dictionary marks this adverb and supplies a study-separately example. Here it modifies the storage predicate, explicitly keeping the copy separate.
source_entries.limits: Source example is not a storage sentence; placement in the new adverbial sequence is an authored composition. It does not specify a filesystem location or grant a recovery guarantee.

source_entries.title: Robert W. Young, English as a Second Language for Navajos: An Overview of Certain Cultural and Linguistic Factors, revised1968, printed168/PDF174, point17
source_entries.sense: When both nouns are stated, the possessor precedes the possessed noun and the latter retains its possessive prefix.
source_entries.grammar: Supports the composed subject Eʼelyaaígíí beʼelyaaígíí, literally image its-copy/image. No invented derivation or suffix is used.
source_entries.limits: General possessed-noun syntax, not a published image-copy software sentence.

source_entries.title: Wilson1994 printed42/PDF28 BEFOREHAND (FROM A PREVIOUS TIME)
source_entries.sense: Particle: beforehand, from a previous time. The next entry separately lists níwohdą́ą́ʼ (in time). Exact nasal-vowel and tone reading must be independently checked; OCR stripped nasality and sometimes first tone.
source_entries.authored_use: Temporal particle qualifies the previously accepted automatic separate storage clause; no nominal previous-draft adjective or relative suffix invented.

source_entries.title: Wilson1994 printed102/PDF58 REPLACE IT, TO; RESTORE IT, TO
source_entries.sense: Second-person form and the example command to restore the sheep to John Yazzie. Not the separate REPAIR entry. Whole command form is retained, not generated from first-person nináánishdlé.
source_entries.authored_use: Source command used as action-topic label before a complete inability sentence, following existing independently accepted NV open/save failure diagnostics. Extending restoration to prior stored image state remains authored; no claim this software clause is source-quoted.

source_entries.sense: Exact first-person inability predicate, verified Young/Morgan1972 printed25/PDF37 and 2019 running primary text. Program speaks as I. No new negation of restored perfective is coined.
source_entries.limits: Present inability after actual attempted failure; not a specific finite past conjugation or permanent impossibility. Prior alleged1958/1972 tonecontrast remains withdrawn as OCRerror.
